overview: This chapter looks at scientific institutions in seventeenth-century England within the map's combined England-and-Ireland record. It also marks the later union of England and Scotland, which did not merge Ireland into Great Britain.

items.text: The Royal Society's first meeting followed Christopher Wren's astronomy lecture in London in 1660. Its members gathered observations, performed experiments and discussed results.
Henry Oldenburg began Philosophical Transactions in 1665. The same year, Robert Hooke published the close observations collected in Micrographia.
The early Royal Society drew members from professional and aristocratic circles and admitted only men. Its meeting rooms represented a restricted part of society.
The English and Scottish Acts of Union created Great Britain on 1 May 1707. The new parliament first met that October.
